items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: He had people in there like Charlie Shavers the great trumpet player, Ziggy Elman was still in the band then, Paul Smith on piano... I stayed with him for three years

ctx.x: Did you give him like a week’s notice this time when you left?

Yeah, I gave him proper notice this time, yeah. I played it straight this time. And after that, Benny was kind of semi-retired then. He was going to go back to New York and not do too much, so that left an opening for me to join Tommy Dorsey in 1947. And that was a great experience, a wonderful band. He had people in there like Charlie Shavers the great trumpet player, Ziggy Elman was still in the band then, Paul Smith on piano, and Tommy himself was just superb you know. I stayed with him for three years, and…

of us said “we have a chance to join Duke Ellington’s band.” So he looked at us and hesitated for about fifteen seconds, then he said “take me with you.” I’ll never forget those words you know. But he was a great man. Harry was a great player and a sensational band besides you know. But I did get a chance to work with him for a while. And then of course after that, of course with Ellington, there are so many stories about that band, and Ellington himself was an element of surprise, always. Because you never knew…

items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: Louie’s an old friend because he was with the Dorsey band when I was there, and we traveled together.

ctx.x: Yeah. I mean he and I had a thing going there that was just — I couldn’t wait to get on the stand at night. Because it kept growing. It started off and the guitar had a lot of things with him when I first joined the thing, and then gradually the guitar was put aside and the piano came in and then pretty soon about half of the show was just him and piano. And it was a challenge all the time. The people would shout a request to him, a tune he didn’t know and I didn’t know, and we’d try to do it. And it was so much…

that time my reading was good so it was no problem. And then when I came back after the two concerts I thought well that’s it. Then I got a call from him and Louie Bellson was playing drums on both the concerts there, and Louie’s an old friend because he was with the Dorsey band when I was there, and we traveled together. I bought a convertible and he and I would travel away from the band, because he’s a non-smoker, non-drinker also, and we couldn’t stand it. I went on the bus once, that was it, with the booze…
